{
  "IP": "neorv32_cpu_regfile",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Architectural integer register state",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_regfile",
      "Information": "The architectural integer register contents are the CPU's persistent operand and writeback state, on which execution depends for preserving and supplying register values.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The register values can contain private or security-relevant CPU data and direct read paths expose them through rs1_o, rs2_o and rs3_o (88-89, 126-127, 141). The write paths allow rd_i to modify the stored register contents when write conditions are met (85-86, 109-110). The CPU depends on these operands, while reset can clear the stored values and write conditions can suppress required updates (85-87, 106-110, 117, 122-127).",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could observe the operand outputs, inject malicious writeback data, or force reset or suppress writes to disclose, corrupt or erase architectural register state.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "rd_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "rs1_o",
        "rs2_o",
        "rs3_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        86,
        110
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        86,
        107,
        110,
        117
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        88,
        89,
        126,
        127,
        141
      ]
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Register-read operand values",

      "Merged Into": "C1",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Writeback register data",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_regfile",
      "Merged Into": "C1",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Register access commands and selections",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_regfile",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The access-command fields and their derived write, address and index signals only select or enable accesses to the register state, so the access-command rule bars them as separate pieces (76-80, 85-89, 109, 126-127, 141, 144)."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset timing",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_regfile",

conceptual assets.information: The architectural integer register contents are the CPU's persistent operand and writeback state, on which execution depends for preserving and supplying register values.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The register values can contain private or security-relevant CPU data and direct read paths expose them through rs1_o, rs2_o and rs3_o (88-89, 126-127, 141). The write paths allow rd_i to modify the stored register contents when write conditions are met (85-86, 109-110). The CPU depends on these operands, while reset can clear the stored values and write conditions can suppress required updates (85-87, 106-110, 117, 122-127).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the operand outputs, inject malicious writeback data, or force reset or suppress writes to disclose, corrupt or erase architectural register state.

considered, not kept.reason: The access-command fields and their derived write, address and index signals only select or enable accesses to the register state, so the access-command rule bars them as separate pieces (76-80, 85-89, 109, 126-127, 141, 144).
Clock and reset inputs and reset chains are explicitly excluded as conceptual assets, although they can affect the kept register state (38-39, 84-87, 106-108, 120-125).
These choices only determine generated implementation structure and register-file features at build time, so no runtime element can modify or withhold them (31-35, 68-149).
